data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["The panel is an active cognitive system, whereas the source contexts often deal with passive data.","The 'single evaluation' constraint is an artificial boundary that makes the problem epistemically interesting but practically solvable with proper design."],"overturn_conditions":["Process-tracing data within the evaluation reveals the causal model.","The single evaluation is designed to include out-of-distribution cases."],"shared_structure":["Under-determination of theory by evidence: multiple mechanisms can produce identical observables.","Distinguishing causal models requires interventions or out-of-distribution testing."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_002","SRC_001"],"transfer_claims":["If the distinction is impossible, then the claim is unfalsifiable within the given constraint.","The only resolution is to relax the 'single evaluation' constraint and require a transfer test.","The argument hinges on whether 'evidence within a single evaluation' can include interventional data."]},"claim":"A genuine reliability gain is fundamentally indistinguishable from mere checklist compliance within a single evaluation if the task outcomes are objectively verifiable and the checklist is fixed, because both mechanisms produce identical observable outputs. The only way to distinguish them is to test transfer to a novel task where the checklist is invalid. Therefore, arguing for or against the claim based on a single evaluation is epistemically underdetermined.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The single evaluation includes process-tracing data (eye-tracking, think-aloud) that reveals the causal model the non-experts are using.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The evaluation includes adversarial cases that effectively act as a transfer test within a single dataset.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The definition of 'single evaluation' is broad enough to include perturbation studies.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If the checklist is causally aligned with the outcome, mere compliance *is* the genuine reliability gain. If the checklist is merely correlational, both the genuine and mere-compliance mechanisms will fail on out-of-distribution cases. Within a single evaluation drawn from the same distribution, the observable behavior (accuracy, calibration, reaction time if measured) will be identical. The distinction requires a manipulation of the checklist's validity, which is not permitted within 'a single evaluation' as typically construed.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
